title: Implement base64url
description:
Implements the URL-safe variant of base64 encoding (RFC 4648 section 5). The decoder is a strict decoder which will error if unsafe components are passed to it.

Add a `url` argument to existing `base64enc()` and `base64dec()` functions.

This is a fast implementation that shares the C-level code, not a wrapper.

title: Use mkCharLenCE with UTF-8 tag in JSON string decode
description: Replaces `Rf_mkString` in the JSON string decoder with `Rf_mkCharLenCE(buf, d - buf, CE_UTF8)`. Avoids a redundant `strlen` on every decoded string and tags the result as UTF-8, consistent with the JSON encoder and CBOR decoder in this package.

title: Replace snprintf hex conversion with table lookup in sb_hash_sexp
description: Replaces per-byte `snprintf("%.2x")` in `sb_hash_sexp` with a 16-entry hex table lookup. Affects the `convert = TRUE` output path shared by sha256/sha3/keccak/shake256/siphash13. No API or behaviour change; NIST vectors still match.

title: Implement JSON
description:
## JSON Encoding/Decoding                                                                
                                                                                        
  This PR adds minimal JSON encoding `jsonenc()` and decoding `jsondec()` designed
   for HTTP API request/response handling. Total ~ 300 lines of C, sharing some code paths
   from the CBOR implementation.                                               
                                                                                        
###  Benefits                                                                              
                                                                                        
  Forgiving parser behavior:                                                            
  - Invalid or malformed JSON returns an empty list `list()` instead of throwing an error         
  - This enables defensive coding patterns where callers can check `length(result) == 0`  
  rather than wrapping in `tryCatch()`
                                                                                        
  R-native type mappings:                                                               
  - NA values (all types) encode as null                                                
  - Length-1 vectors encode as scalars; length >1 encode as arrays                      
  - Named lists → objects; unnamed lists → arrays                                       
  - Deep nesting protection (max 512 levels)                                            
                                                                                        
 ### Non-conformance with RFC 8259 (decoder only)                                                        
                                                            
  - Invalid JSON returns an empty list instead of erroring.                             
  - Duplicate keys are preserved; R accessors (`$`, `[[`) return first match.               
  - Non-standard number forms may be accepted (e.g., leading zeros, hexadecimal).       
  - Invalid escape sequences are output literally (e.g., \uZZZZ becomes "uZZZZ").       
  - Incomplete Unicode escape sequences for emoji are tolerated.

title: Implement CBOR
description:
## CBOR (RFC 8949) encoder/decoder for R
 
 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8949.html
 
 Supports a minimal subset:
   - Major type 0: unsigned integers
   - Major type 1: negative integers
   - Major type 2: byte strings (raw vectors)
   - Major type 3: text strings (UTF-8)
   - Major type 4: arrays (lists)
   - Major type 5: maps (named lists)
   - Major type 7: simple values (false, true, null, undefined), float32 and float64

title: Implement Base58Check
description: Adds a 4-byte checksum suffix (double SHA-256) to the data before base58 encoding. Note: does not include a version byte prefix (unlike Bitcoin Base58Check).
